Ava: Heads up — after yesterday's kernel rollout I started seeing quality regressions on long-context decode when KV is stored as INT8. Latency wins are real (~10-12% p50) but a non-trivial fraction of outputs have weird token drift after ~800 tokens. Dumping traces now.

Ravi: Same on canary. Throughput improved but top-1 token divergence vs fp32 baseline goes up ~1.7% on long-prompts test set. Attaching a tiny sample where the model invents an extra sentence mid-doc.

Lina: Ugh. Do we know if this is calibration-related or a math-path change from the new int8 matmul kernel? My hunch: scale mismatch for KV accumulation + changed accumulation order.

Ava: Preliminary profile shows noise appears right after the kernel switch at layer 26 (mid-decode). p95 latency slightly lower but p99 tail jittered.

perf-bot: Automated perf snapshot (canary-07):
```
model: redwood-2-small
seq: 2048
batch: 4
kv-format: INT8
kernel-swap: enabled
decode: tokens/sec: fp32-kv=360, int8-kv=410
p50 latency: -12% vs baseline
token-divergence: +1.8% (long-prompts-v2)
mem: -34% KV footprint
```

Maya: Possible culprits: 1) quantization scales not being recomputed for the new kernel path 2) per-layer vs fused-scale mismatch 3) reduced accumulator precision when using mixed-int path. Also check tiny-batch behavior — batching heuristics might be nudging us into a less numerically-stable kernel.

Ravi: I pulled a raw trace. Kernel selection log shows we pick int8_fast for sequences > 512 and batch>=2. For some long prompts we flip kernels mid-request due to dynamic batching boundaries which could change rounding. Snippet:
```
[2026-06-12T14:05:23Z] select_kernel: layer=26 seq=1024 batch=3 -> int8_fast
[2026-06-12T14:05:23Z] select_kernel: layer=27 seq=1100 batch=1 -> int8_fallback
```
The switch seems to coincide with the divergence spike.

Lina: That switching is bad if the kernels use different accumulation conventions. We should either ensure ABI-compatible accumulation / scaling or prevent mid-request kernel swaps. Short term: force stable kernel for entire request.

Ava: Agreed. Two short experiments: A) force int8_fallback (more conservative accumulator) for any request with seq>1024; B) re-run quant calibration with longer calibration sequences (calib_set=long-prompts-v1, 2k tokens) to produce per-channel scales.

Ravi: I'll run A/B on staging. Script I'm using:
```
# run canary with stable-kernel enforcement
./deploy_canary.sh --cluster kv-canary-07 --env STABLE_KERNEL=1 --kv-format=INT8
./run_eval.sh --eval-set long-prompts-v2 --capture token-diffs --profile
```
ETA ~2h.

Maya: Also try a hybrid FP8 fallback for layers > 30 — FP8 KV reduced memory benefit but might keep decode quality while we debug.

perf-bot: Job queued: regression-4521 (A/B: stable-kernel vs calibrated-scales).

deploy-bot: Canary deployed to kv-canary-07 with STABLE_KERNEL=1 (build r2843).

Lina: If stable-kernel fixes quality but regresses latency too much, we can try a no-switch policy per-request: allow int8_fast only if all layers in request pick it, otherwise fallback to int8_fallback for whole request. That keeps throughput gains for compatible requests.

Ava: Good plan. @Ravi please include per-layer kernel-choice trace and token-level diffs. Also rerun with FP8-KV variant to compare decode noise vs mem/latency tradeoffs.

Ravi: Will do. Kicking off now. Will post results to thread in ~2h.

Ava: Thanks — tagging long-prompts-v2 eval owners: @Lina and @Maya for follow-up on calibration. :thumbsup:

Maya: Understood, I'll prepare a long-calib set and a calibration pipeline tweak (per-channel scales + outlier clipping).

perf-bot: regression-4521 started. ETA 90m.

Ravi: Quick update: initial A run (stable-kernel) restored token divergence to +0.2% and p50 latency is +4% vs the int8_fast rollout. Posting detailed traces after full run.

Ava: Nice. If consistent, we can ship a kernel selection policy change: no mid-request kernel swaps + calibrate-int8-long.

deploy-bot: Canary autoscaling note: kv-canary-07 scaled from 3->5 pods during tests.

Lina: Nice progress. We should add a unit test in kernel-selector to assert deterministic kernel choice per-request given sequence & batch plan. I'll open a PR.

Ravi: Opening PR for logging-level export and per-request kernel policy now.

Ava: Thanks everyone. Keep updates short in this thread.
